Figure 2-3 Representation of main MTV dimensions in meters Final Technical Report 14/57 3 MAIN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS AND ENVIROMENTAL CONDITIONS 3.1 Technical Requirements The MTV design will be fabricated to the agreed design requirements considering relevant standards as well as its intended testing, accreditation, operation, and maintenance plans, ensuring accordance with the IEC TC 114 Technical Specifications, specifically TS 62600-200 and TS 62600-300 [2] . This standard defines the power performance assessment requirements for CECs. The MTV shall be designed to have the following characteristics as defined in the SOPO [1]: - Twenty-year design life - Lifting capabilities for deploying and recovering turbines in a safe and controlled manner - Onboard power generation - Onboard data acquisition system - No propelled but capable of being transported via open ocean towing up to sea state (SS) 3 - Anchoring and mooring system designed for current speeds and water depths at all proposed test sites - Adhere to all applicable o International regulations (International Maritime Organization, IMO) under ABS as Classification Society o U.S. Coast Guard regulations The MTV has been designed to have the following testing capabilities specified in the SOPO [1]: - Test rotors 3-8 m in diameter at design maximum current speeds - Capable of supporting measurements on turbine blade loads, motions, and rotor thrust that are correlated with flow characteristics such as turbulence and shear - Characterize system performance under off-axis flow conditions - Perform component and system maintenance tests - Perform relevant deployment and retrieval tests - Perform power quality measurements - Dissipate power in load bank(s) based on a maximum number of turbines and design conditions - Provide a non-grid connected test barge with a grid emulator for testing CECs under various loads/fault conditions - Test control systems - Test system load shedding under high flow conditions - Compatibility to hold test visualization of blade and tip vortex cavitation -
